claim: Replacing the constant start (R=2/3) with a generic (1+1) multiplicative hill-climber on 200 step heights raised R from 0.666667 to 0.809855; the winning shape is a smooth unimodal bump (largest/mean height 4.36, no zeros) whose f*f is strongly peaked (11% of knots within 1% of max, max at 0.693 of support). This is the best result of generation 1 and shows the constant is not a local maximum for

A smooth-bump start plus coordinate-wise multi-scale hill-climbing with restarts (200 steps, no zeros, largest/mean 2.11) reached R=0.795839 from the constant start, confirming that bell-shaped profiles beat 2/3 by a wide margin even with a less aggressive climber than p0007.

Multi-resolution hill-climbing on step heights (50 up to 6400 steps) raised R from 0.666667 to 0.763044; the resulting f*f is notably flatter than the p0007/p0006 bumps (only 10.97% of knots within 0.1% of max vs 3.99%/5.49%), suggesting flatter f*f tops trade off against peak height in a way the climber can exploit at coarse resolution.

A piecewise-constant 'table' shape (flat top of half-width a, shoulders of height c out to b) with grid search plus refinement and hill climb reached only R=0.720735, below the smooth-bump results (0.7958-0.8099). The flat-top hypothesis that shoulders raise f*f tails enough to beat a Gaussian is not supported: the best table has largest/mean height only 1.79 and f*f max at 0.497 of support.

A Gaussian-width search (a in [0.1,100], N=1000) followed by hill-climb refinement produced 215 negative heights and was rejected; the multiplicative perturbation step (factor = 1 + step*N(0,1)) can drive heights negative, so any climber using multiplicative noise must clamp to non-negative values.

A coordinate hill-climber with an off-by-one in the quadrature padding (Lp of length len(L)+1 assigned L of length len(L)) crashed with a broadcast error (99 into 98); the correct padding is len(L)+2 with zeros at both ends, as used in p0002/p0007.

Replacing coordinate hill-climbing with exact-gradient Adam ascent plus multi-scale upsampling (N=200->400) and perturbed restarts raised R from 0.795839 to 0.919251 (+0.1234), the largest single gain seen; the winning shape is sparse (36.8% zeros, max/mean 15.91) with a much flatter f*f top (23.2% of knots within 0.1% of max vs 3.99% for the peaked bump). Exact analytic gradients beat stochastic

Adding coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps (factors 1.3/1.1/1.03 both ways) as the main stage on top of p0007's climber raised R from 0.809855 to 0.826691 (+0.0168) at N=200, keeping the smooth no-zero bump (max/mean 3.84) but shifting the f*f max to 0.610 of support. Systematic per-coordinate line search beats random single-coordinate moves on the same shape.

Optimizing only the first half of a symmetrized profile (mirror-reconstructing the full shape each evaluation) with a multiplicative line search at N=400 raised the table-shape start from 0.720735 to 0.735771 (+0.0150), but this symmetric family (max/mean 2.26, f*f max at 0.481) stays far below the asymmetric peaked results (0.81-0.92). Symmetry is not competitive with the peaked/sparse shapes.

Upsampling p0007 to N=400/800 and continuing the (1+1) multiplicative coordinate climber produced no change (0.919251 -> 0.919251, +0.0000): the run started from p0008's already-optimized N=400 state and the climber could not improve it. Resolution alone (N=200->400->800) does not raise R once the shape is near a local optimum; the optimizer, not the grid, is the binding constraint.

Adding a coordinate-descent line search (multipliers 0.6-1.6 plus additive offsets, noise restarts) on top of p0008's gradient ascent gave no gain (0.919251 -> 0.919251, +0.0000). Once exact-gradient Adam has converged, coordinate line search on the same N=400 grid finds nothing further, indicating a genuine local optimum rather than a plateau.

The best results (0.9193) come from sparse, high-contrast shapes (37% zeros, max/mean ~16) with a very flat f*f top, while all smooth-bump families plateau at 0.81-0.83. Whether the true optimum is sparse (support-restricted) rather than smooth is untested: worth starting from a sparse/compactly-supported profile and optimizing with exact gradients to see if R exceeds 0.92.

Fixing the objective to the exact official (2A+B)/3 quadrature and its exact gradient (dq=(4/3)L+shifted/3) on top of p0008's Adam ascent raised R from 0.919251 to 0.921043 (+0.0018) at N=400, keeping the sparse high-contrast shape (32.5% zeros, max/mean 16.2). The gain is small because p0008's shape was already near-optimal for the true functional; the wrong (A+B)/3 objective had merely mis-scale

Annealed power-mean soft-max (p=4..128) replacing the hard max in the denominator, with the corrected (2A+B)/3 gradient, gave no gain over p0008 (0.919251 -> 0.919251). Spreading the max penalty did not help: the hard-max run p0019 with the same corrected objective did gain (+0.0018), so the soft-max smoothing itself was the limiting factor, not the flat-top ill-conditioning.

A low-dimensional 'pedestal plus edge blocks' family (2-4 rectangles, Nelder-Mead, N=800, exact score) reached only R=0.826479 from a fresh start, well below the 0.9193 sparse-shape results. The block family's f*f is not flat enough (10.6% of knots within 0.1% of max vs 23-26% for the winners) and max/mean is only 4.46, so a few rectangles cannot reproduce the high-contrast sparse optimum.

A block-mutation climber with a multi-scale upsample ladder (800/1600/3200) crashed with 'TypeError: only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python scalars' because math.exp was applied to an array (sigma * rng.standard_normal(w) with w>1). Block mutations must use np.exp, not math.exp, when the perturbation is vector-valued.

Exact-gradient Adam ascent with multi-scale upsampling (400->6400) and perturbation restarts, applied to p0010's N=200 multiplicative-sweep result, raised R from 0.826691 to 0.865339 (+0.0386) at N=400; the shape stayed smooth (19.2% zeros, max/mean 3.55) with a very flat f*f top (37% of knots within 0.1% of max). A quasi-Newton step on the same objective does not move the converged point, so the p0019 plateau is not an optimizer-strength artifact of Adam's unit-normalized gradients.

Pixel-wise exact-gradient Adam refinement (N=400, 4 perturbed restarts, final polish) from p0018's rigid U-shape (pedestal + edge blocks) raised R from 0.826479 to 0.876302 (+0.0498), but the result is a different, non-flat basin: only 15.86% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max (vs 26-28% for the p0019 line) and ||f*f||_inf = 2.35 (vs 0.815). Small but real: restart diversity at fixed N pays a little where upsampling does not.

Replacing O(N^2) coordinate-descent scoring with an O(N) local-update version and reordering stages to run coordinate descent early and repeatedly after gradient steps raised R from 0.919251 to 0.920514 (+0.0013) at N=400. Making the coordinate sweep cheap enough to interleave with gradient ascent recovers a gain that a single post-Adam sweep (F11) did not.

Exact-gradient Adam ascent with multi-scale upsampling and smooth perturbation restarts from p0010's N=200 coordinate-sweep result raised R from 0.826691 to 0.879392 (+0.0527) at N=400, producing a very sparse shape (73.2% zeros, max/mean 23.83) with a sharply peaked f*f (12.98% of knots within 0.1% of max, ||f*f||_inf = 2.98). Small-N perturbation restarts pay where large-N upsampling does not.

Rewriting the ascent loops with cheap time checks every 16 iterations and prioritizing fixed-N polish before multi-scale/perturbed restarts raised R from 0.922923 to 0.923141 (+0.000217) at N=400 on p0024's state; the gain came from spending the budget on native-resolution polish rather than upsampling, keeping the sparse shape (33.2% zeros, max/mean 18.07).

N=400 is not resolution-limited: high-resolution random constructions land in smooth low-contrast basins (max/mean 3.46, 19.7% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max) rather than the sparse high-contrast optimum.
